name: Textron
description: Textron builds Cessna and Beechcraft private jets, turboprops and trainers (Textron Aviation), Bell helicopters and tiltrotors including the MV-75 (Bell), and defense systems (Textron Systems). Its Industrial segment is a different business: Kautex plastic fuel tanks and clear-vision systems for carmakers, plus E-Z-GO golf cars, turf-care and ground-support vehicles. Aircraft are sold one-time at delivery, with a growing aftermarket of parts and service; Bell and Systems work on US government contracts. Total backlog was $18.8B at the end of 2025.

gics.note: Conventional filing: GICS sector and sub-industry as listed on Wikipedia 'List of S&P 500 companies' (read 2026-10-01); the list does not show the industry group or industry. SEC SIC code 3720 (Aircraft & Parts) per EDGAR. About 22 percent of revenue is Industrial (auto fuel systems, golf cars, turf equipment), which does not fit the aerospace label.

hq.note: Providence, RI per EDGAR business address and Wikipedia S&P 500 list

employees.note: About 34,000 worldwide, 80 percent in the US; about 7,700 US employees (29 percent) are union-represented. FY2025 10-K

businessLines.name: Textron Aviation
businessLines.how: Customers buy each aircraft at delivery (list prices in the millions), then pay for parts, maintenance and service over the aircraft's life; sold through its own sales force and independent representatives.
businessLines.description: Cessna and Beechcraft business jets, turboprops and military trainers (T-6, AT-6), plus parts and service including the Hawker brand.

revenue.note: FY2024 $5,284M (+13 percent): aircraft revenue +$548M, aftermarket +$123M. Backlog $7,724M (-2 percent).

businessLines.revenueNote: FY2024 $5,284M (+13 percent): aircraft revenue +$548M, aftermarket +$123M. Backlog $7,724M (-2 percent).

operatingProfit.note: Segment profit; FY2024 $566M. Share of $1,363M total segment profit (computed).

businessLines.name: Bell
businessLines.how: US Government and allied militaries pay under multi-year contracts as work is performed; commercial helicopters are sold per aircraft plus parts and service.
businessLines.description: Military and commercial helicopters, tiltrotor aircraft, spare parts and services; primary US programmes include MV-75 and military sustainment.

revenue.note: FY2024 $3,579M (+20 percent); military aircraft and support revenue +$570M (28 percent) on MV-75 and sustainment. Backlog $7,795M (+4 percent); a $1.3B MV-75 prototype testing and evaluation award in 2025.

businessLines.revenueNote: FY2024 $3,579M (+20 percent); military aircraft and support revenue +$570M (28 percent) on MV-75 and sustainment. Backlog $7,795M (+4 percent); a $1.3B MV-75 prototype testing and evaluation award in 2025.

operatingProfit.note: Segment profit; FY2024 $370M (-2 percent) on higher R&D

businessLines.name: Industrial (Kautex and Textron Specialized Vehicles)
businessLines.how: Kautex sells parts under long-term supply relationships to automaker OEMs per vehicle built; Specialized Vehicles sells vehicles through independent distributors and dealers to golf courses, municipalities, businesses and consumers, plus used golf cars after refurbishment.
businessLines.description: Kautex: plastic fuel systems, clear-vision and cleaning systems, battery enclosures for automakers (over 30 plants in 13 countries). Specialized Vehicles: E-Z-GO golf cars, utility vehicles, turf-care and ground-support equipment.

revenue.note: FY2024 $3,515M (-9 percent); Textron Specialized Vehicles revenue -$294M (18 percent) largely from a disposition

businessLines.revenueNote: FY2024 $3,515M (-9 percent); Textron Specialized Vehicles revenue -$294M (18 percent) largely from a disposition

businessLines.name: Textron Systems
businessLines.how: US Government and allied customers pay under contracts; backlog $3,304M (+27 percent).
businessLines.description: Defense and government systems and services.

businessLines.name: Finance
businessLines.description: Captive finance arm that finances customer purchases of Textron aircraft.

businessLines.name: Textron eAviation
businessLines.how: Small light-aircraft sales; mostly a research cost centre.
businessLines.description: Pipistrel electric and light aircraft and sustainable-aviation R&D; from fiscal 2026 mostly folded into Textron Aviation.

brands.name: Cessna and Beechcraft (including Citation, King Air, Caravan)
